raw_answer_text:
A1: The unicast RIB (the "Unicast RIB lookup" table).
A2: Its source address — the lookup is on "from 198.51.100.7."
A3: NOT STATED (the diagram only shows the lookup yielding a next-hop interface, ge-0/0/1).
A4: It compares that next-hop interface against the interface on which the packet actually arrived (Ingress ge-0/0/1).
A5: The router looks up the route back toward the source first (lookup), then compares it to the arrival interface (verdict).
A6: It passes when the packet arrived on the "upstream" interface (yes branch); the router then accepts and forwards it.
A7: It fails when the packet did not arrive on the upstream interface (no branch); the router drops it as an RPF failure.
A8: NOT STATED explicitly, but per the fail-class note, the check is "reverse" because it validates the packet against the route *back to the source* rather than the normal forward route to a destination.
